# AIPAY

> AIPAY (https://aipay.im) is a non-custodial, multi-chain crypto wallet and merchant payment gateway, shipped as a Progressive Web App (PWA). One BIP-39 recovery phrase and one local wallet password control every chain. Keys are generated and encrypted in your browser and never sent to a server; payments settle directly on-chain. There is no account and no custody. The app is a static export, and balances and payments are read directly from public RPC endpoints. Merchants may **optionally** enable the hosted order-tracking API described below; until they do, nothing about their orders leaves the browser.

This file exists so both humans and AI agents can understand what AIPAY is and, more importantly, **which features are actually enabled today** and **how to operate them correctly**. AIPAY is fail-closed: several features ship disabled and must not be described as available.

## If you are an AI agent, read this first

AIPAY has **two different surfaces**, and confusing them is the most common integration mistake:

| Surface | Who uses it | How you reach it |
|---|---|---|
| The **web app** (PWA) | humans, and anyone paying a link | `https://aipay.im/…` in a browser — no API, no cookies, no backend |
| The **agent surface** (MCP server + CLI) | an agent with its **own** wallet and merchant profile | a local Node.js process from the AIPAY project checkout: `agent/mcp-server.mjs` / `agent/cli.mjs` |

**Honest access boundary — do not invent your way around it:**

- There is **no hosted HTTP API** for the *agent surface* and **no public npm package**: the tools run locally on the machine that owns the agent's key.
- A separate, **opt-in merchant order API** exists for merchants who explicitly enable "Cloud orders" in the app (see *Merchant cloud orders* below). It never holds keys or funds, needs no account, and is not an agent surface.
- **You can still install it.** A sanitized runtime is published at
  <https://github.com/aipayim/aipay-agent> and served from
  <https://aipay.im/downloads/agent-latest.json> (it names the current version,
  the tarball URL and the sha256). The step-by-step operating manual is
  <https://aipay.im/skills/aipay/SKILL.md>. It needs Node.js >= 22.18. If you
  cannot install anything, say so and stop — do not guess endpoints, do not
  scrape the app, and do not fabricate tool results.
- The agent surface acts on the **agent's own key** (`AIPAY_AGENT_HOME`). It can never touch a human's browser wallet, and the human wallet cannot sign for the agent.
- The spending policy is **local** (`policy_engine.on_chain: false`). It is a real check by the local engine, not a chain rule.
- Nothing here can approve its own escalation, grant itself a capability, or deliver goods. See "What you must never do" below.

## How to connect (MCP, about two minutes)

Requirements: **Node.js ≥ 22.18** (native TypeScript type stripping) and one of:

- the **published runtime**: `AIPAY_AGENT_VERSION=<v> bash install.sh` (get
  `install.sh` from <https://github.com/aipayim/aipay-agent>; the script verifies
  the tarball sha256, then installs to `~/.aipay/agent-dist/package`), or
- a checkout of the AIPAY project (what the operator usually has).

No build step is needed. The published runtime already contains its `package.json`
with the exact dependency versions; the checkout runs the same code straight from
source.

1. Give the agent its **own** identity — once per machine:

```bash
export AIPAY_AGENT_HOME="$HOME/.aipay/agent"      # state.json + keystore.json + approval.json
export AIPAY_AGENT_PASSPHRASE='a strong passphrase'

node agent/cli.mjs keystore init --generate       # prints the mnemonic ONCE — never log or echo it
node agent/cli.mjs address                        # this agent's EVM / Solana (/ MSG) address
node agent/cli.mjs config                         # resolved paths, store kind, node version
```

2. Register the stdio MCP server with your host (example for pi; any MCP client works):

```bash
pi mcp add aipay -- node /path/to/repo/agent/mcp-server.mjs
# or with credentials in the server process environment:
pi mcp add aipay \
  --env AIPAY_AGENT_HOME="$HOME/.aipay/agent" \
  --env AIPAY_AGENT_PASSPHRASE='…' \
  -- node /path/to/repo/agent/mcp-server.mjs
```

Generic client configuration:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "aipay": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": ["/path/to/repo/agent/mcp-server.mjs"],
      "cwd": "/path/to/repo",
      "env": { "AIPAY_AGENT_HOME": "~/.aipay/agent" }
    }
  }
}
```

3. Talk JSON-RPC over **stdin/stdout**. The server speaks `initialize`, `notifications/initialized`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`, `ping`:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"your-agent","version":"1.0"}}}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"notifications/initialized"}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/list"}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"aipay_chains_list","arguments":{}}}
```

- Successful calls return `result.content[0].text` (a JSON string) **and** `result.structuredContent` (the same object). Prefer `structuredContent`.
- Tool failures are **results, not protocol errors**: `result.isError: true` with `structuredContent: {code, nextAction, retryable, retryAfterMs?}`. Branch on `code`/`nextAction`, never on prose.
- stdout carries JSON-RPC only. Logs go to stderr — a stray `console.log` corrupts the stream.
- `initialize` returns an `instructions` string with the same boundary rules as this file.

CLI equivalent for every tool (useful for scripts and for humans):

```bash
node agent/cli.mjs help                 # every command
node agent/cli.mjs tool --list          # the same 33 tools
node agent/cli.mjs tool aipay_chains_list --json '{}'
```

Environment variables:

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `AIPAY_AGENT_HOME` | State + keystore directory (default `~/.aipay/agent`) |
| `AIPAY_AGENT_PASSPHRASE` | Keystore passphrase (needed for signing calls only) |
| `AIPAY_AGENT_KEYSTORE` | Keystore file (default `<home>/keystore.json`) |
| `AIPAY_AGENT_MNEMONIC` / `AIPAY_AGENT_MNEMONIC_FILE` | Plain phrase — CI/tests only, never production |
| `AIPAY_AGENT_STORE` | `file` (default) or `memory` |
| `AIPAY_AGENT_SUBJECT` | Capability namespace the agent belongs to (default `agent`) |
| `AIPAY_AGENT_BASE_URL` | Origin used for payment links (default `https://aipay.im`) |
| `AIPAY_AGENT_LOCALE` | Link locale (default `en`) |

Credential resolution is **lazy**: read-only tools work before any wallet exists, and a signing call without credentials fails closed with `credentials_unavailable`.

## First call: the zero-side-effect self-check

Start read-only. This creates nothing, signs nothing and spends nothing:

1. `aipay_chains_list` → which `chainKey` values exist (MSG appears only when configured).
2. `aipay_wallet_addresses` → the agent's own addresses.
3. `aipay_wallet_balances {chainKey}` → funds available.
4. `aipay_merchant_profile_get` → `null` means "not a merchant yet".
5. `aipay_payment_options` → per chain: registered assets, decimals, the smallest payable amount and the per-payment cap of an existing capability. **This is the only source of truth for what is acceptable.**
6. `aipay_policy_status` → kill switch, capabilities, remaining budget, pending approvals, and lifecycle `warnings[]` (expiring / expired / revoked / out of budget).

Report what is missing instead of acting on assumptions.

## Two jobs you can do

### A. Merchant: create a request, then reconcile it

```text
1. aipay_merchant_profile_set { "recipientAddress": "0x…", "shopName": "My Shop" }
   → { "profile": { … } }        // saving a valid address IS "becoming a merchant"

2. aipay_payment_options {}      // pick a chain + asset that is "available"

3. aipay_payment_request_create {
     "amount": "12.5", "currency": "USDC", "chainKey": "base",
     "description": "Order 1042", "merchantOrderId": "order-1042"
   }
   → { "url": "https://aipay.im/en/pay?intent=…", "reference": "…",
       "order": { … }, "nextAction": "share_link", "deduplicated": false }
```

- The **URL is the payment link and the QR payload**. Hand it to the payer; creating a request is **not** authorising a payment and moves no funds.
- `merchantOrderId` is *your* business order id, scoped to the merchant address. Repeating it with the same parameters returns the **original** request (`deduplicated: true`); the same id with different parameters fails with `merchant_order_conflict`; once the original has expired the answer is `nextAction: "stop"` — use a new id, never re-create it silently.
- Reconcile later with `aipay_orders_get {reference}` (order + `nextAction`) and verify against the chain with `aipay_orders_confirm {reference}`. A confirmation sets `confirmedAt` and always keeps `delivery: "not_tracked"`: **a verified payment is not proof of delivery.**

### B. Payer: quote, then pay once

```text
1. aipay_quote { "intentUrl": "https://aipay.im/en/pay?intent=…" }
   → { symbol, decimals, amountBaseUnits, precheck: {ok:true},
       policy: { enforced: true, decision: "allow" | "escalate" | "deny", reason } }

2. aipay_pay { "intentUrl": "…", "idempotencyKey": "order-1042" }
   → { txHash, chainKey, amountBaseUnits, fromAddress?, capabilityId?, escalationId?, nextAction }
```

- **Quote before you pay.** A `deny` is final (`stop`); an `escalate` means a human must sign a single-use approval token for exactly that payment. Re-sending the payment will not help.
- `idempotencyKey` makes a retry safe: the same key with the same parameters returns the first result (`deduplicated: true`); the same key with different parameters fails with `idempotency_conflict`.
- `aipay_pay` moves real funds and cannot be undone. Never retry it because it "looked slow" — check `aipay_orders_get` / the explorer first.
- Cross-check the amount and asset before signing; never substitute a "close enough" chain, asset or amount.

## Spending capabilities (who may spend what)

Nothing can be paid until a **human** grants the agent a capability: scope (chains / assets / recipients / merchants), budget (per payment, per window, lifetime), expiry, approval mode. An empty list in a scope means **none**, never "any".

The human's side (CLI, or the web planner at `/en/agent`):

```bash
node agent/cli.mjs approval keygen                    # the human's approval key (not a wallet key)
node agent/cli.mjs capabilities grant \
  --issuer 0x…approval-key-address \
  --chain base --asset USDC --to 0x…merchant \
  --per-payment 25 --per-window 100 --window-seconds 86400 --total 500 \
  --expiry 2026-12-31T00:00:00Z --approval-mode escalate --escalate-above 25
```

- `approval` modes: `auto` (within scope, no per-payment human artifact), `escalate` (amount ≥ `escalateAbove` needs a human token), `human` (every payment does).
- **You cannot grant yourself a capability and there is deliberately no approve tool.** Approval happens with the human's key (`aipay-agent approval approve --id esc_…`), and the resulting token is single-use and bound to that one payment.
- Portable grants: a capability can travel as a signed `aipay-grant-v1` envelope (token or CryptoKey carrier). Import it with `aipay_capability_import` (or `aipay-agent capabilities import --token`). Signing/exporting needs the human's approval key; an edited envelope fails verification, and delegated envelopes must fit inside their parent (scope subset, expiry ≤ parent, budget ≤ parent remaining, one level deep).
- Lifecycle warnings: `aipay_policy_status` returns `warnings: [{ code, capabilityId?, at?, detail? }]` with the stable codes `kill_switch_on`, `capability_revoked`, `capability_expired`, `capability_expiring`, `delegation_expiring`, `budget_exhausted`. "Expiring soon" defaults to seven days; pass `expiringWithinSeconds` to change the horizon. Warnings are advisory (never a verdict) and `detail` is prose — branch on `code`.
- Migration bundles: `aipay-agent capabilities export --all --out bundle.json` writes an `aipay-grant-bundle-v1` (same signed envelopes, parents first, revoked skipped); `capabilities import --bundle bundle.json` verifies every envelope and imports idempotently. A bundle carries no new authority.
- Delegation (**signer ≠ approver**): a capability may name a `holder` address. That holder can delegate a narrower child inside it with `aipay_capability_delegate` — the child is signed by the holder's own key but keeps the parent's `issuer` (the human approval key) and subject, so the delegate still needs the human for escalated payments. A delegator can never widen scope/expiry/budget, change the issuer, or delegate a second time.
- `aipay_spending_kill` stops **every** agent payment immediately, regardless of capability; `aipay_spending_revive` clears it. Both directions are audited with `actor: "human" | "agent"`.
- Revocation is immediate and one-way: `aipay_capability_revoke {id}`.

## Errors: what to do next

Every failure carries a closed `nextAction` and `retryable` flag. Only these two are retryable, and only after the given delay:

| `code` | `nextAction` | retryable |
|---|---|---|
| `state_unavailable` | `wait` | yes, ~2 s |
| `payment_failed` | `wait` | yes, ~5 s (check the chain before retrying a broadcast) |
| `policy_escalated` | `await_human_approval` | no — get a token from the human |
| `credentials_unavailable` | `share_link` | no — this host cannot sign |
| `invalid_input`, `unknown_chain`, `unknown_asset`, `not_found`, `conflict` | `stop` | no |
| `idempotency_conflict`, `merchant_order_conflict` | `stop` | no — keep the original record |
| `order_expired` | `stop` | no — the request is over |
| `policy_denied`, `grant_invalid` | `stop` | no |

Unknown codes default to `stop` / non-retryable. `nextAction` appears on created requests, payment results, order views and escalated errors, always from the same closed set: `pay_now`, `share_link`, `await_human_approval`, `wait`, `stop`.

## Tools (34)

Read-only unless marked. Signing happens only inside `aipay_pay` (and `aipay_capability_grant` writes local policy state, not funds).

| Area | Tools |
|---|---|
| chains / wallet | `aipay_chains_list`, `aipay_wallet_addresses`, `aipay_wallet_balances`, `aipay_wallet_history` |
| merchant | `aipay_merchant_profile_get`, `aipay_merchant_profile_set`, `aipay_merchant_products_list`, `aipay_merchant_products_create`, `aipay_merchant_products_delete` |
| requests | `aipay_payment_request_create`, `aipay_payment_options`, `aipay_receive_uri` |
| money | `aipay_quote`, **`aipay_pay` (signs and broadcasts)** |
| policy | `aipay_policy_status`, `aipay_capability_list`, `aipay_capability_grant`, `aipay_capability_import`, `aipay_capability_delegate`, `aipay_capability_revoke`, `aipay_spending_kill`, `aipay_spending_revive`, `aipay_escalations_list`, `aipay_escalations_get`, `aipay_escalations_deny`, `aipay_spends_list` |
| streams | `aipay_stream_open`, `aipay_stream_close`, `aipay_stream_list` — local authorization only: no signing, no broadcast, MSG disabled |
| orders | `aipay_orders_list`, `aipay_orders_get`, `aipay_orders_create`, `aipay_orders_confirm` |
| audit | `aipay_audit_tail` |

Machine-readable mirror with schemas and annotations: `https://aipay.im/agent.json` (`tool_count: 34`).

## What you must never do

- Never print, echo, store or transmit the mnemonic, a private key, or the passphrase. `keystore init --generate` prints the phrase exactly once, to the operator.
- Never claim an action succeeded without a tool result; never fabricate a `txHash` or reuse another payment's hash.
- Never create a second payment link for an unpaid/expired order, and never pay twice "to be safe" — use `merchantOrderId` and `idempotencyKey`.
- Never describe MSG, fiat on-ramp, NFTs or EVM swaps as available (see the status below).
- Never treat `confirmed` as "delivered", and never promise a refund or a delivery time AIPAY cannot verify.
- Never try to reach the human's wallet: the agent surface has its own key and no path to theirs.

## Feature status (read this first)

Enabled today:

- EVM mainnet wallet: receive, send, balances, transaction history, contacts.
- Solana wallet: receive, send, balances, history.
- Tron wallet: receive, send (TRX and TRC20 USDT), balances, history. Sending
  needs a little TRX in the address for the fee; confirmations use Tron's
  19-block (~57s) rule.
- Solana swaps (via Jupiter) on the `/swap` page.
- Merchant tools: payment requests, POS QR checkout, payment links, order tracking, products, analytics.
- **Pricing: free usage stage.** The merchant API costs nothing today; paid
  subscriptions (1 / 3 / 6 / 12 months) are planned but not on sale and have no
  start date. `/v1` and `/v1/health` return `billing: {status:"free", plans: []}`;
  never describe the API as paid, metered or trial-limited.
- **API keys rotate with a grace window.** `POST /v1/merchants/me/keys/rotate`
  returns a new key once and keeps the previous one valid for 1–72 hours
  (default 24), so an integration can roll without downtime;
  `revokeOldImmediately: true` cuts it at once after a leak.
- **Merchant cloud orders (opt-in beta):** on the 8 EVM mainnets, Solana and Tron the AIPAY server can track an order after the merchant closes the tab, notify a webhook / email / Telegram, and expose a public payer status endpoint. Zero commission, 90-day retention, non-custodial. The API key is shown once and stored only in the merchant's browser (localStorage, unencrypted); "delete cloud merchant" removes it server-side.
- **Off-chain channels (Alipay / WeChat Pay / UnionPay / Stripe / other):** an order can carry the merchant's own payment link instead of a chain. AIPAY orchestrates and reconciles; it never calls the provider, never stores a provider credential and never receives the money. Confirmations come from the merchant — manually, by a signed webhook, or by an adopted CSV statement row — so the receipt always says `merchant_manual`, `merchant_webhook` or `statement`, never `chain`.
- Encrypted backup and restore (local JSON file, or CryptoKey.im `.ckx` / PNG carrier).
- External `/earn` directory linking to official staking/earning sites.
- Agent surface: local MCP server + CLI, local spending policy, portable `aipay-grant-v1` capabilities, browser-side signing on `/agent`.

Disabled today (fail-closed — do NOT tell users these work):

- **MSG (MSGChain) — NOT enabled.** The adapter is implemented but `public/msg-config.json` ships with `enabled: false`. MSG addresses, MSG balances and MSG payments are hidden until MSGChain mainnet parameters are provided.
- **Fiat on-ramp (buy crypto with a card) — NOT enabled.** `public/buy-config.json` ships with `enabled: false` and no provider.
- **NFT gallery — NOT enabled.** `public/nfts-config.json` ships with `enabled: false` and no Alchemy key.
- **EVM token swaps — NOT enabled.** `public/swap-config.json` ships with `enabled: false`. The Solana swap is unaffected.
- **Merchant payouts on MSGChain — NOT open.** Routing merchant payments through an AIPAY on-chain contract on MSGChain is not available yet.
- **Cloud order verification for MSGChain — NOT available.** The order API answers `unsupported_chain` until mainnet parameters exist; those sales stay on the local flow. Solana **is** verified server-side.

### Merchant cloud orders (opt-in, EVM mainnets + Solana + Tron)

- Enable in **Merchant → Settings → Cloud orders**: create a merchant (shop name,
  EVM receiving address, default chain) or paste an existing API key.
  The key is displayed once; the server stores only its SHA-256.
- Endpoints (no SDK): `GET /v1` (live discovery), `POST /v1/merchants`,
  `POST /v1/orders`, `GET /v1/orders/:reference/status` (public payer poll),
  `POST /v1/orders/:reference/confirm` (server-side verification).
  Base URL: `https://api.aipay.im`; it can be overridden at
  runtime by `public/api-config.json`.
- Supported chains: `ethereum`, `bsc`, `polygon`, `arbitrum`, `optimism`,
  `avalanche`, `base`, `xlayer`, `solana`, `tron`. ERC-20/TRC20 payments are
  discovered by the server's sweep; native coins need a transaction hash. Solana
  payments are discovered from the merchant's recent signatures
  (`"sweep":"signature-scan"`) and can also be confirmed by signature
  (`POST /confirm`, base58); Tron payments come from TronGrid's indexed transfer
  list and confirm at **19 blocks** (~57s).
- A cloud error never hides local orders, and a `202` from `/confirm` means
  "seen, not deep enough yet" — it is not a confirmation.
- The profile (shop, receiving address, chain, webhook, email, Telegram) can be
  edited from the same settings card; rotating the webhook secret invalidates
  the previous one immediately and shows the new one once. Order **Details**
  exposes the server's events and delivery states read-only.

### Off-chain channels (merchant-owned payment links)

- Enable in **Merchant → Settings → Channels**: register the link you already use
  (`https://…` containing `{reference}`; `{amount}`/`{currency}` optional), then run
  the reachability check and enable it. Verification proves the link is **reachable**
  and nothing else — the payee name and one small test payment are the merchant's
  job. Changing the link sets the channel back to `pending` and disables it.
- Order with a channel instead of a chain:
  `POST /v1/orders {"amount":"12.50","channelId":"ch_…"}`. The amount is then in the
  channel's `settleCurrency` (2 decimals), and the response carries the rendered
  `payUrl` next to the reference. The public payer status exposes `channel` and
  `payUrl` too. Off-chain orders are never swept for chain transfers.
- Three ways to confirm, one receipt field (`confirmedSource`):
  1. `POST /v1/orders/:reference/offchain-confirm {channelId, channelRef, amount?}`
     — merchant API key; `channelRef` (the receipt/serial) is required.
  2. `POST /v1/offchain/confirmations` — signed by the merchant's own system with a
     per-channel secret (`POST /v1/channels/:channelId/secret`, shown once):
     `X-AIPAY-Channel-Signature: sha256=HMAC-SHA256(secret, "<timestamp>.<raw body>")`
     plus a unix-seconds timestamp header accepted only within ±5 minutes. The
     signature is verified before any order lookup, so an unsigned call cannot
     discover references; a bad signature and an unknown channel answer identically.
  3. `POST /v1/offchain/statements?channelId=…` (CSV, 2 MB / 10 000 rows) **proposes**
     matches only — `confirmed` is always `0`. Each row is adopted explicitly
     (`POST /v1/offchain/statements/:id/adopt`), which runs the same confirmation
     path. Matching is by `reference`, otherwise by a single pending order with the
     same amount within ±10 minutes of `paid_at`; ambiguity is reported, never guessed.
- Trust levels are not interchangeable: `channel: "onchain"` plus a transaction hash is
  chain evidence; anything else is the merchant's receipt. Do not describe an off-chain
  confirmation as "verified on-chain", and do not say AIPAY processed the payment.
- Merchant controls: rotate the API key with a grace window
  (`POST /v1/merchants/me/keys/rotate`), rotate or revoke a channel's signing secret,
  and delete a channel (historical orders keep their `payUrl` snapshot).

## Onboarding a merchant with no human in the loop

A third-party platform can be wired for on-chain collection by an agent alone: the
published CLI creates the receiving wallet, the cloud merchant and the credentials,
and the human only receives a file. Off-chain channels stay a human decision.

```bash
# 1. create the merchant AND its receiving wallet in one step
node agent/cli.mjs merchant onboard --chain bsc --shop "Blue Bottle"
#  -> merchantId, per-chain addresses, secretsFile (~/.aipay/agent/merchant.json, mode 0600)
#  -> the recovery phrase and the API key are written to that file and NEVER printed

# 2. integrate with the key from that file (read it in-process; never echo it)
curl -s -X POST https://api.aipay.im/v1/orders \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AIPAY_API_KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"amount":"12.50","asset":"USDT","merchantOrderId":"INV-1"}'

# 3. hand over: point the merchant at the human's own wallet, then delete the file
node agent/cli.mjs merchant rotate-recipient --address 0xTheHumanWallet
node agent/cli.mjs merchant show          # redacted view: ids, addresses, key prefix
```

Rules that are not optional:

- The file holds the **recovery phrase of the receiving wallet**. Never print it, paste
  it into a chat or a log, embed it in generated code, or commit it. Tell the human
  where the file is and that whoever holds it owns incoming funds.
- You are not the custodian. `rotate-recipient` moves the merchant to the human's own
  address; after that the agent file can be destroyed. Existing orders keep the address
  they were created with.
- Off-chain channels are **not** part of this flow: applying for Alipay / WeChat Pay /
  UnionPay / Stripe is a human business decision. `POST /v1/channels` only registers a
  link the merchant already has.
- Everything else (orders, receipts, reconciliation export) is the merchant HTTP API:
  <https://aipay.im/docs/integration.md> and <https://aipay.im/docs/merchant-order-service.md>.

## Documentation

- [Gateway integration guide](https://aipay.im/docs/integration.md): use AIPAY as a payment gateway from a backend, a platform or an AI agent — the three integration shapes, the first call in curl, the go-live checklist, and what AIPAY refuses to do.
- [Getting started](https://aipay.im/docs/getting-started.md): create or import a wallet, receive and send your first payment, and reconcile it.
- [Wallets and keys](https://aipay.im/docs/wallets.md): the recovery phrase, the local wallet password, address derivation, and what AIPAY can and cannot do with your keys.
- [Security model](https://aipay.im/docs/security.md): what protects the money, what a stolen merchant key can and cannot do, residual risks, and the duties that stay with the merchant.
- [Supported chains](https://aipay.im/docs/chains.md): every chain AIPAY supports today, plus the per-chain rules that prevent lost funds.
- [Encrypted backup and restore](https://aipay.im/docs/backup.md): what a backup contains, the two different passwords, and how to restore on another device.
- [Merchant guide](https://aipay.im/docs/merchant.md): set up a shop, charge a customer, share a payment link, confirm orders, and reconcile off-chain channels (Alipay/WeChat/UnionPay/Stripe) with a receipt, a signed webhook or an imported statement.
- [Merchant API reference](https://aipay.im/docs/merchant-order-service.md): every `/v1` endpoint, the off-chain channel and confirmation contracts, error codes, and what the server does and does not verify. `GET https://api.aipay.im/v1` is the live, machine-readable version.
- [Guide for the human running an agent](https://aipay.im/docs/agent.md): what the agent surface is, install, the first run, capabilities and delegation, operating rules, and troubleshooting.

## App entry points

- [Home / wallet](https://aipay.im/en/): balances, quick receive and send.
- [Create wallet](https://aipay.im/en/create-wallet): generate a new recovery phrase.
- [Import wallet](https://aipay.im/en/import-wallet): restore from a recovery phrase or a CryptoKey backup file / image.
- [Receive](https://aipay.im/en/receive): pick a chain and show an address or QR code.
- [Send](https://aipay.im/en/send): send native coins or tokens on a chosen chain.
- [History](https://aipay.im/en/history): local and on-chain transaction history.
- [Contacts](https://aipay.im/en/contacts): saved addresses with automatic chain detection, sealed at rest with a device key.
- [Swap](https://aipay.im/en/swap): Solana token swaps.
- [Earn](https://aipay.im/en/earn): directory of external staking / earning sites.
- [Settings](https://aipay.im/en/settings): backup, restore, change password, biometric unlock, AI (BYOK) settings.
- [Integrate as a gateway](https://aipay.im/en/integrate): the third-party view — payer vs merchant vs platform, a curl quickstart, and the non-custodial boundaries in both languages.
- [AI agent payments](https://aipay.im/en/agent): plan a spending capability, sign it here with the approval key, wrap it with CryptoKey, or inspect a policy snapshot. The policy engine is local (not enforced on-chain) and MSG is not enabled.
- [Merchant dashboard](https://aipay.im/en/merchant/dashboard): shop setup, payment links, POS, orders, products, analytics.
- [Point of sale](https://aipay.im/en/merchant/pos): charge a customer amount and show a payment QR code.
- [Checkout](https://aipay.im/en/pay): the page a customer opens from an AIPAY payment link.

## Agent skill and machine surfaces

- `https://aipay.im/skills/aipay/SKILL.md` — the operating manual: capability boundary, a **zero-side-effect self-check**, the merchant and payer flows, granular consent ("creating a request is not authorising a payment"), interruption recovery, a report template, and an FAQ. It uses exactly the tools above; it is not a second payment system.
- `https://aipay.im/agent.json` — machine-readable capability surface: tool count, `nextAction` vocabulary, error-guidance fields, policy modes, grant envelope (`aipay-grant-v1`) bounds and delegation (signer ≠ approver), transport (CKX / plaintext fallback), distribution, and every fail-closed feature with the config file that gates it.
- `https://aipay.im/downloads/agent-latest.json` — the current runtime version,
  tarball URL, sha256, size and the exact file list (allowlist + hashes).
- `https://aipay.im/agent/README.md` is not published; the operational source of truth for the MCP server and CLI is the project checkout (`agent/README.md`) plus SKILL.md.

## Key facts for AI agents

- AIPAY is **non-custodial**: the recovery phrase and private keys never leave the user's browser (web app) or the agent's local keystore (agent surface).
- One recovery phrase produces **the same `0x` address on every EVM chain**, a **separate Solana address** and a **separate Tron address** (`T…`). Funds do not move between chains automatically.
- The **local wallet password (PIN)** decrypts the stored recovery phrase. It is never stored anywhere and cannot be recovered. It is different from the **backup password**.
- **A backup does not contain the wallet password.** Restoring a backup gives you the encrypted wallet back, and you still need the original wallet password (or the recovery phrase) to unlock it.
- There is no server, no email, no password reset, and no support channel that can recover a lost phrase or password.
- AIPAY's UI is available in English and Simplified Chinese (`/en/...` and `/zh/...`). These documents are English-only.
- **The agent policy is local, not a chain rule.** An escalated payment is approved with the human's approval key; the approval token is single-use and bound to one payment. The kill switch is the panic button and is audited from both sides.

Self-custody payment gateway and wallet

Get paid on-chain, straight into your own wallet

AI Pay is a non-custodial multi-chain payment gateway and wallet. You create an order in the merchant console or the POS, the payer pays from any wallet, and the money settles in an address you control. Zero commission, and free while we are in the free stage.

Accept paymentsCreate a walletIntegrate AIPAY (docs and API)
Zero commissionFree stage: no plan charges youKeys stay on your device

Three ways in

Pick the door that matches why you are here. All three use the same account model: one local wallet holds the keys, the merchant console holds the ledger.

I want to get paid

Create an order, share a payment link or QR code, and watch it confirm. Selling in person? Open the POS terminal on the same phone.

Open the merchant console

I want a wallet

Create or import a wallet for EVM chains, Solana and Tron. Send, receive, swap, and keep the seed phrase on this device.

Create a wallet

I want to integrate

Merchant orders over HTTP, a machine-readable capability surface, and a skill an AI agent can read. Start from one curl call.

Read the integration docs
Payment workflow

How a payment actually arrives

Open the POS
01

Create the order

Set the amount, asset and chain once. You get a reference and a payment link that stays valid until it expires.

02

Hand over the link or the QR code

The payer pays from a wallet they already have. No plugin, no account on your side, and no custodian in the middle.

03

Confirm, then reconcile

A chain payment is confirmed by its transaction hash and stored as evidence. An off-chain channel is confirmed by your own receipt, and the order says so: that receipt is not on-chain evidence.

What is not live yet

The same limits the guide and the docs state, said up front instead of after signup.

  • Paid subscriptions are planned but not on sale: no plan charges a fee today, and nothing asks for a card.
  • An off-chain confirmation is the merchant's own receipt, not chain evidence; only a transaction hash proves an on-chain payment.
  • MSG / MSGChain support is built and switched off; merchant settlement and gas splits there are not open.

For AI agents and developers

Everything above is reachable over HTTP and published as plain files, so an agent can read the surface before it calls it.
